'''Marlis Rahman''' (9 June 1942 – 28 July 2018) was an Indonesian politician and academic. He served as [[List of governors of West Sumatra|Governor of West Sumatra]] for eight months between 2009 and 2010, and before that as the province's vice governor between 2005 and 2009. He was previously the [[Rector (academia)|rector]] of [[Andalas University]].
==Early life and academic career==
Rahman was born on 9 June 1942 in [[Bukittinggi]], as the youngest of five children. His father was Malin Batuah, a cart driver, and his mother Lian was a housewife. He completed his elementary, middle and high school educations in state schools in Bukittinggi, before continuing his studies to [[Andalas University]]. While in Andalas, he was active in the student body, and later the organizations [[KAMI (Indonesia)|KAMI]] and the [[Muslim Students' Association (Indonesia)|Muslim Students' Association]].<ref name="pilgub">{{cite book |title=Pemilihan Umum Gubernur dan Wakil Gubernur Sumatra Barat Tahun 2010 |work=Issuu |date=2010 |publisher=[[General Elections Commission]] |pages=6–7 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230114001353/https://issuu.com/indosiana/docs/3_buku_pilgub_2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="sumbarsatu">{{cite news |title=Marlis Rahman, Anak Tukang Padati dan Akademisi Itu, Tutup Usia |url=https://sumbarsatu.com/berita/18796-marlis-rahman-anak-tukang-padati-dan-akademisi-itu-tutup-usia |access-date=15 January 2023 |work=Sumbarsatu |date=28 July 2018 |language=id-ID}}</ref> He was later sent to the [[Bandung Institute of Technology]] to complete his degree, and he obtained his bachelor's in Biology in 1970.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VJFuAAAAMAAJ&q=marlis+rahman+unand+biologi |language=id}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=Direktori alumni Institut Teknologi Bandung |date=1992 |publisher=[[Bandung Institute of Technology]] |page=666 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dP_F8LkMe7wC&q=marlis+rahman+itb |language=id}}</ref> He then worked in the biology department within Andalas, becoming the department secretary in the mid-1970s.<ref>{{cite web |title=Profil Jurusan Biologi |url=http://biologi.fmipa.unand.ac.id/images/Download/Booklet/Profil-Prodi-Biologi.pdf |publisher=[[Andalas University]] |access-date=15 January 2023 |page=29 |language=id}}</ref> In 1977, he became the school director at the Semen Padang High School.<ref>{{cite web |title=Warta SP edisi 59 |url=http://www.semenpadang.co.id/warta/59/files/basic-html/page4.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180704184917/http://www.semenpadang.co.id/warta/59/files/basic-html/page4.html |access-date=15 January 2023 |archive-date=2018-07-04 |language=id}}</ref> 

In 1978, Rahman became the dean of Andalas' faculty of natural sciences, and remained so until 1983.<ref name="fmipa">{{cite web |publisher=[[Andalas University]]|title=Pimpinan Fakultas |url=https://fmipa.unand.ac.id/profil/pimpinan-fakultas.html |access-date=15 January 2023 |language=id}}</ref> He later continued his studies at [[Ohio University]], receiving his master's in botany and later a PhD in 1989.<ref name="sumbarsatu"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Rahman, Former Governor of Sumatra, Passes Away |url=https://www.ohio-forum.com/2019/05/alumni-news-rahman-former-governor-of-sumatra-passes-away/ |publisher=[[Ohio University]] |access-date=15 January 2023 |date=13 May 2019}}</ref> Returning to Andalas, he continued to serve as faculty head between 1990 and 1994.<ref name="fmipa"/> In 1997, he became the university's [[Rector (academia)|rector]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Sejarah Ringkas |url=https://old.unand.ac.id/id/sejarah.html |publisher=[[Andalas University]] |access-date=16 January 2023 |language=id}}</ref>

==Political career==
Rahman ran as the running mate to [[Gamawan Fauzi]] in West Sumatra's 2005 gubernatorial election, with the pair winning 41.54 percent of votes in a five candidate race. They were sworn in on 15 August 2005.<ref>{{cite news |title=Gubernur Sumbar Dilantik |url=https://news.detik.com/berita/d-422434/gubernur-sumbar-dilantik |access-date=16 January 2023 |work=detiknews |date=15 August 2005 |language=id-ID}}</ref>

On 23 October 2009, Fauzi resigned as governor due to his appointment as [[List of Ministers of Home Affairs (Indonesia)|home affairs minister]], and Rahman became the province's acting governor.<ref>{{cite news |title=Marlis Rahman Menjabat Gubernur Sumatera Barat |url=https://nasional.tempo.co/read/204342/marlis-rahman-menjabat-gubernur-sumatera-barat |access-date=16 January 2023 |work=Tempo |date=25 October 2009 |language=id}}</ref> He was officially sworn in as governor by Fauzi on 7 December 2009, the ceremony taking place at the provincial council building's parking garage as its main room was still damaged from the [[2009 Sumatra earthquakes|September earthquake]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Gubernur Sumbar Dilantik di Garasi Mobil |url=https://www.jpnn.com/news/gubernur-sumbar-dilantik-di-garasi-mobil?page=2 |access-date=16 January 2023 |work=JPNN |date=7 December 2009 |language=id}}</ref>

He ran as a gubernatorial candidate in the 2010 gubernatorial election, but placed second in the five-candidate race with [[Irwan Prayitno]] instead becoming governor.<ref>{{cite news |title=Kilas Balik Pemilihan Gubernur Sumbar Sejak 2005 |url=https://langgam.id/kilas-balik-pemilihan-gubernur-sumbar-sejak-2005/ |access-date=16 January 2023 |work=langgam.id |date=9 December 2020 |language=id}}</ref>

==Later life and death==
Rahman died on 28 July 2018 at his home in Padang. Although he was provided with a state funeral and his body was to be brought to the governors' office, this was cancelled due to his family's request. He was buried at a nearby cemetery in Padang.<ref>{{cite news |title=Marlis Rahman Dikebumikan Tanpa Penghormatan Terakhir |url=https://www.jawapos.com/jpg-today/28/07/2018/marlis-rahman-dikebumikan-tanpa-penghormatan-terakhir/ |access-date=15 January 2023 |work=[[Jawa Pos]] |date=28 July 2018 |language=id}}</ref>
